$comment: Hand-curated corrections to the schema-derived Molang path catalogue. Merged last by apps/vscode/tools/build-molang-paths.mjs; notMolang and knownParseGaps are read by apps/vscode/tools/check-molang-paths.mjs. Every entry says why.

add.reason: Render-controller conditions ({"controller.render.x": "query.is_powered"}); no Blockception marker. Many vanilla client entities.
Keys of scripts.variables are the variables being declared public; the values ("public") are not Molang.
Spelled with a capital axis letter in the vanilla magma cube; the schemas only list scalex/scaley/scalez.
The game joins the array into one program: vanilla husk/zombie/piglin pre_animation opens a block in one element ("(v.melee_spear_equipped) ? {") and closes it several elements later ("};").
Same scripts block as the client entity: statements, joined into one program.
Same scripts block as the client entity (vanilla bow: "wield_first_person_pull": "query.main_hand_item_use_duration > 0.0f && c.is_first_person"); Blockception's attachable schema lacks it.
Same scripts block as the client entity.
Same scripts block as the client entity.
Same render-controller condition form as the client entity.
Keys are item identifiers, values the condition under which this attachable applies (vanilla armour: "query.owner_identifier == 'minecraft:player'").
Keys are bone-name globs, values pick the material ("variable.is_enchanted ? Material.enchanted : Material.default", "Array.materials[query.is_invisible]"); no Blockception marker.
Keys are bone-name globs, values the visibility condition; the most common Molang field no schema marks (about 200 vanilla instances).
Array elements are resource references (Texture.x, Material.x, Geometry.x) that the geometry/materials/textures expressions index into.
Keys declare the Array.x names the expressions refer to.
Legacy per-axis rotation list, [{"y": "180.0 - this"}, {"x": "query.body_x_rotation"}], used by the vanilla squid; not in any schema.
BP entity animate conditions; Blockception types them as plain strings.

set_property values are Molang for int/float/bool properties (vanilla creaking: "math.clamp(query.property('minecraft:creaking_swaying_ticks') + 1, 0, 6)"); for enum properties a plain value. Reached through nested sequence/randomize, hence **.
Condition choosing the ambient sound (vanilla allay: "query.is_using_item"); Blockception types it as a plain string.
Documented by Mojang as a number or Molang expression, like rotate_rider_by next to it.
Curve names are the variables the curve is read through ("variable.shrink").
Event nodes nest through sequence/randomize to any depth; Mojang's schema is recursive there, so the walk sees one level only.
Sound-variant selector in sounds.json, evaluated on the entity and returning the variant name ("query.is_baby ? 'baby' : query.property('minecraft:sound_variant')"); no schema marks it.
Condition choosing a feature, documented by Mojang as Molang; no Blockception marker.

patch.reason: Statements run on the parent before it renders (they set variables); Blockception titles it Molang Number.
An enum property's default is a plain value ("unrolled", "default"); int/float/bool defaults may be Molang.
A condition, though Mojang's schema types it as a general expression.
Runs statements on the spawned effect (sets its variables); not an animation value.

remove.reason: The values are access modifiers ("public"); the keys are the Molang names (added as target key).
Timeline values are event names, not Molang (a description mentions Molang).

notMolang.reason: Geometry identifiers ("geometry.agent") bound to short names that render controllers reach as Geometry.<short name>. The dotted form looks like the geometry. namespace but is a resource id.
Geometry identifiers, as for the client entity.
